# 0109 — Direct transactions have independent logical controllers

Date: 2026-09-27
Type: ISF execution architecture
Owner: SEMANTIC-INTROSPECTION-MCP-FRONTIER.32.1.3.3.1.2.2
Status: selected; implementation and qualification remain open

## Context

The retained direct-controller audit strict-admits and compiles independent
transactions but executes only the first declaration. Reversing declarations
reverses reachability. Plain local calls separately free-run an unguarded callee
or strand a waiting caller. Authored public IAL0 references demonstrate separate
control registers over shared actor storage, including repeated calls and reset.
Those references are feasibility evidence, not implemented ISF lowering.

The binding audit also distinguishes three timing classes. Generated `do`
inputs are live handoffs and correctly reject snapshot spelling. Local rule
payloads are snapshots, but at decision time the pulse-gated mux lost the value before
a delayed read. A request-gated target completes once and reads zero; changing
only the emitted mux default to its retained source restores the expected read.
An ungated rule target is a separate authored free-running control, not evidence
that rule fan-in implicitly installs an entry guard.

Evidence: `docs/audits/direct-controller-contract-20260927.json` and
`docs/audits/direct-controller-binding-timing-20260927.json`.

## Decision

Represent each retained transaction as an explicitly owned logical controller.
Its states, initial entry, transitions, local storage and activation effects
belong to that transaction and clock domain. Actor state retains its single
owner under decision `0107`; a controller does not acquire a private copy of
actor storage. Independent eligible transactions can make concurrent progress.
Declaration order cannot choose which transaction exists at runtime.

Use private per-controller state registers and guarded decision-tree bodies
through the existing public IAL0 carrier. This is an implementation-neutral
state/transition contract, not a new public language or backend bypass. A
single-controller optimization is acceptable only with proven semantic parity.
Generated selectors, widths and names are private, collision-safe and reset
under the owning module's qualified reset contract. Do not invent a reset for
an unqualified no-reset configuration.

Keep source-owned logical state identities in schedules and provenance.
Explicit ownership must survive expansion, call wiring, domain partitioning,
priority analysis and emission; do not recover it by splitting name prefixes.
Translate logical state predicates through the controller mapping, including
rule/transaction priority conditions. Preserve point-active assignments,
assertions, monitors, waits, loop edges and terminal holds. Raw textual
replacement across expressions, state names, type/member names and messages
is not an acceptable identity migration.

### Activation and binding boundaries

- Ordinary authored `on` guards remain entry conditions. Returning to entry
  reevaluates the guard; this repair does not convert every level condition
  into an edge trigger. Uncalled transactions without an entry guard retain
  their authored free-running semantics.
- A blocking local call owns its callee request entry. Install that entry if
  absent, as required for a callable body; preserve body ordering and entry
  sampling. One held request accepts one invocation. Fresh delayed completion
  releases the caller, and request release permits the next invocation.
  Reset aborts partial work and clears the activation history consistently.
- Local rule fan-in continues to produce the documented request signal.
  Preserve authored target guards, including `(on transaction_start)` and
  explicit qualifications; do not infer a new entry solely from a rule target.
- Local call input snapshots belong to the admitted invocation. Resolve caller
  operands in caller scope, capture at the qualified activation boundary, and
  retain values through waits. Callee formal names resolve in callee scope.
  Copy output bindings only under that invocation's completion condition.
- Rule payload snapshots must retain the accepted payload through the body.
  Preserve visibility on the acceptance edge as well as later reads; adding
  a register that delays an entry sample is not an equivalent repair. Source
  selection must follow actual admitted requests and existing resource grants.
- Generated `do` and spawn live handoffs stay live. Generated trigger payload
  retention keeps its separately qualified timing. Do not turn specialization
  parameters into mutable payload signals or silently convert timing classes.
- No request queue, stack, recursive invocation, simultaneous-caller ownership
  or busy-request payload replacement is inferred. Qualify repeated/nested
  acyclic calls, request release, early samples and reset explicitly. Unproved
  competing activation ownership needs a precise boundary and an owned repair.

### Shared-write admission

The old single encoded state variable cannot prove mutual exclusion between
independent controllers. Before enabling them, derive physical writer targets
from scoped identities and preserve source owner/state provenance. Classify
storage, actor outputs, partial/bank updates, named drives, binding copies and
generated handoffs under their real ownership rather than only bare LHS text.

Disjoint owners/targets need no arbitration. Preserve already qualified
completion-pulse fan-in and rule/resource behavior. Potentially overlapping
data writers require a sound existing compatibility or exclusion proof;
otherwise fail with an actionable conflict before claiming executable support.
Do not silently pick declaration order, suppress a controller, serialize work,
or treat parsed transaction/transaction priority as implemented arbitration.
Existing rule/transaction priority remains assignment-local; it is not a
whole-transaction grant or a stalled-progress protocol.

### Rollout and signoff

Start with a shadow logical-controller/consumer model under the existing
region/effect doctrine (`0013`). Prove unchanged source and public reports
before switching execution. Resolve direct formal identities under `.49.2.2`,
then repair local payload retention and establish shared-write admission before
independent execution is promoted. Separate local-call entry/capture and broad
backend/report qualification leaves retain their own runtime obligations.

Use declaration permutations, overlapping short/long independent work,
repeated and nested calls, changed inputs after acceptance, early entry samples,
held requests, reset during work, state-active priority and named-point checks.
Compare exact native/API/MCP reports and public IAL0 replay. Significant control
migration requires the broader regression gate; admission, lint and authored
reference simulations alone cannot close production runtime qualification.

## Consequences

The current direct-controller warning remains until generated production HDL
passes the owned repair gates. Local rule payload retention is now integrated
and qualified under .32.1.3.3.1.3.2 (T1965/T1966), including entry samples,
busy/reset/held requests and granted multiple sources. Independent controllers
and local-call timing remain open. Generated live-call probes stay separate
positive controls; they do not prove snapshot support. The early ungated
trigger probe is retained with its corrected interpretation.

This selects execution and admission boundaries without claiming an implemented
controller, arbitration protocol, scoped-port repair or storage-access feature.
The original rollout also placed passive register-access metadata behind those
execution repairs. That sequencing is narrowed on 2026-09-30 under SEM `.38.1`:
the SPECFORGE R1-R3 contract expressly requires unchanged scheduled FSM and HDL.
Parser declaration metadata, the detached declared-storage snapshot and schedule
JSON projection can satisfy it without touching controller or writer admission.
Exact before/after carrier and HDL controls are required for that separation.
The director has prioritized blocked downstream feature requests. Execution
repairs remain mandatory for their affected runtime claims; passive metadata
delivery does not qualify, hide or close them.

# 0110 — Actor storage variables reject HDL keywords

- Date: 2026-09-27
- Type: language contract
- Status: accepted
- Owner: SEMANTIC-INTROSPECTION-MCP-FRONTIER.49.2.2.3.2.2.2.3.2.2.2.2.2.2.2.2.1.3

## Context

A public strict ISF check accepted `(var cell (width 4))` and emitted `cell`
as a register and generated child input. Independent Verilator compilation
rejected those declarations because the spelling is a SystemVerilog keyword.
The parser checked only identifier shape. The shared registry already knows
this keyword, but decision 0027 applied it only to child instance labels.
Four recent formal-preparation controls consequently checked strict carriers
without proving their keyword-named HDL compilable.

## Decision

Actor storage `var` and `variable` names must be simple identifiers and must
not be reserved by the shared shipped-target keyword union. SystemVerilog
matching remains case-sensitive; VHDL matching remains case-insensitive.
Reject at source parsing with actor, variable name, reserving target and rename
guidance. Keep one backend-neutral source identity; do not silently rename or
introduce target-specific escaping for authored storage names.

A bank name is a logical owner, not an emitted signal spelling. Its element
names use numeric suffixes, so keyword logical names remain admitted when
the actual scalarized names satisfy the existing collision/shape contracts.
Field metadata likewise does not become an independent authored register.

## Consequences

Invalid variable sources now produce an early classified failure instead of
apparently successful invalid HDL. Legal non-keyword source/report/HDL names
remain unchanged. Formal-preparation controls use `value_reg`, with separate
keyword-negative coverage and independent legal-control compilation.

This bounded contract extends 0027 only for ISF actor storage variables; other
identifier families and direct FSM declarations retain their separately owned
contracts. It does not claim global HDL identifier completeness or extend
storage access metadata. The original compiler failure stays retained under
the owning task, alongside the independently isolated read-guard defect.

# 0111 — Same-value selector fan-in is compatible

- Date: 2026-09-28
- Type: backend and semantic report contract
- Status: accepted
- Owner: SEMANTIC-INTROSPECTION-MCP-FRONTIER.32.1.3.3.1.3.3.2.2.3.2.2.2.2.2.2

## Context

Strict ISF admission accepts equal-value writes with matching timing. The
generated backend groups their source enables into one RHS value family and
ORs those enables. T1974 nevertheless fails a generated SystemVerilog
`$onehot0` assertion when an admitted rule and transaction both select `9`.
The emitted data selection is unambiguous; the assertion imposes exclusivity
that the source and value-family contracts do not require. T1211 previously
checked the assertion text without executing that allowed overlap.

## Decision

An analyzed same-RHS selector family permits concurrent source enables. Its
legacy `same_value_assertion` metadata key remains, with the existing key
shape and source list; `kind => compatible_fanin` identifies that policy.
No source-exclusivity assertion is emitted for this policy. Consumers must
read the policy kind instead of assuming that every legacy assertion field
describes a one-hot obligation.

Distinct RHS value-family enables retain `multi_value_assertion.kind =>
onehot0` and the corresponding SystemVerilog check. Explicit `onehot0`
metadata still renders that obligation. Standalone decision-tree and shared
composition ownership/exclusivity contracts use their separate producers and
are unchanged. Verilog continues to emit no SystemVerilog assertions.

## Consequences

This corrects a metadata value and emitted verification policy without changing
report key families, source admission, data muxes, priority masks or scheduling.
Same-value family entries remain discoverable under `selector_conflict_targets`
for report compatibility; their presence alone does not mean an exclusivity
assertion exists. Different-value checking remains mandatory.

The original executed failure and its public reconstruction stay sealed in
`docs/audits/priority-contributor-repair-20260928/`. Static contract repair
precedes separately owned observed positive/negative execution. That execution
must allow the compatible control and reject a deliberately broken
different-value mask before complete priority runtime signoff. No runtime
assertion flag or process-admission rule is disabled.

# 0112 — ISF reset provenance is separate from hardware policy

- Date: 2026-09-30
- Type: ISF source and public report contract
- Status: accepted; provenance implemented under .60.3.3.1
- Owner: SEMANTIC-INTROSPECTION-MCP-FRONTIER.60.3.2

## Context

SPECFORGE must distinguish a reset stated by an input specification from a
compiler-selected implementation default. The supplied unstated-reset packet
is retained with current public products in
`docs/audits/specforge-unstated-reset-20260930/`. Legacy reset omission and an
explicit asynchronous active-low `rst_n` produce identical hardware and reports
apart from source paths. A clock-only named domain instead selects hardware
without reset or a guaranteed initial state. These are different choices.

`explicit_system_contract` describes the emitted FSM carrier. It cannot serve
as evidence that the ISF author wrote a reset clause. Changing defaults or
inventing startup initialization would change existing source semantics and
would not answer the provenance question.

## Decision

Retain declaration provenance before parser defaults. Add `reset_provenance`
to schedule JSON and optional `source.reset_provenance` to successful native
check and semantic JSON for directly parsed ISF inputs. The same values must
reach the public adapter and actual newline MCP responses. Existing reset
policy fields, source acceptance, scheduled FSM and HDL stay unchanged.

The value is an array in authored domain order. Each entry has exactly
`domain` and `origin`. A legacy actor has one entry with `domain: null`.
Named-domain actors use the declared domain names. The origin values are:

| Origin | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `explicit` | A reset clause occurs in this ISF actor/domain. |
| `legacy_default` | The legacy actor omits reset and selects the documented default. |
| `domain_absent` | The named domain omits reset and selects hardware without it. |

`explicit` proves clause presence only; flat-name polarity inference and omitted
timing/polarity operands still follow existing rules. This metadata does not
prove a fact about an upstream specification that FSMGen has never read.
SPECFORGE must preserve its own grounding evidence.

Unknown provenance in a caller-constructed actor must remain unknown: schedule
JSON uses null rather than guessing from an effective reset object. Direct FSM
and other source formats do not gain ISF provenance. Parsing/check failure does
not manufacture successful source provenance. Advertise the optional shared
source field and schedule field/entry/value families in their capability
contracts, with complete discovery and public-query tests.

For the downstream question, an omitted legacy reset is the existing form for
an unstated ISF reset **with the documented implementation default selected**.
The new metadata makes that selection visible. Clock-only domains are suitable
only when deliberately selecting hardware without reset. No existing form
defers reset kind/polarity to instantiation; this answer does not claim one.
If SPECFORGE requires a deferred hardware decision rather than a visible
default, it must retain that unresolved source fact before executable ISF
generation. The director clarified that this ticket is a question. A configurable reset
feature is outside its scope; the inferred follow-on `.61` is superseded.
Absence must not be silently implemented as reset-free hardware.

## Delivery and qualification

Implement provenance retention, detached projection and shared report fields
in one bounded slice; generated products must match the retained baseline after
removing only the added metadata and generated date banner. Cover explicit and
omitted legacy forms, defaulted clock, single and mixed named domains, source
permutation, caller-constructed actors without evidence, and malformed source.
Qualify parser/scheduler, native check/semantic/schedule, API/newline and
capability discovery. Since hardware must be unchanged, this metadata slice
does not require a new native simulator run or waive its existing admission.

The final downstream response must disposition every supplied question and
expected outcome, include a runnable omission example and exact field meaning,
and keep the initialization and VHDL limits explicit. This provenance change
does not depend on independent transaction controllers, writer admission, or
the unresolved historical native `setpgid` cause.

# 0113 — ISF record interface ports reuse packed type and writer contracts

- Date: 2026-09-30
- Type: ISF language, lowering and public report contract
- Status: input authoring admitted; complete input/output and consumer qualification remain open
- Owner: `SEMANTIC-INTROSPECTION-MCP-FRONTIER.60.4.2`

## Context

The preserved SPECFORGE request is `docs/audits/specforge-aggregate-intake-20260930/packet.json`.
Its required R1–R3 ask for declared packed record inputs/outputs, scalar field access, whole
same-type port/storage copies, and visible type/layout metadata. R4 list-root ports and R5 variant
records are optional. The intake's current refusals are historical evidence, not a new regression
oracle after delivery.

At selection, the parser admitted aggregate aliases only on storage variables. Lowering already
preserves interface type references in `+size`; core `.fsm` type/path machinery owns packed
representation. Generated internal storage handoffs do not establish authored aggregate-port
support. Decisions `0107` and `0109` retain state ownership, physical writer admission and execution
qualification. R13/R14 require stable public reports and ordered IAL1 → IAL0 lowering; this feature
must not add a second type system or bypass IAL0.

## Decision

### Source and value contract

Select `(input NAME (type T))` and `(output NAME (type T))` for an existing actor-local or imported
package-qualified alias resolving to a packed record. Reuse the existing recursive record/list
member type system, including nested members. Root list ports remain R4. Unknown types, malformed
declarations, unresolved/nonpacked types and unsupported carriers fail before successful lowering,
with the port/type/context identified. Width/type exclusivity, closed options, declaration presence
and existing domain ownership remain. Typed output reset/default options remain outside this request
and retain their current explicit refusal.

Input fields are live scalar reads in each already-supported scalar expression context: transaction
conditions, set/update RHS, rules and named drives. Existing explicit sampling remains the way to
request a snapshot. Resolve paths against the declared root type; unknown members, non-scalar leaves
and out-of-range nested items fail contextually. Do not infer fields by punctuation or admit
whole-record truthiness, arithmetic or subaggregate writes.

Whole copies involving a record port require the same resolved record type: compare recursive kind,
member names/order and scalar width/signed/state-model properties under the existing type resolver;
equal packed width alone is insufficient. Alias spelling may differ when it resolves to that same
type. Support input-to-storage and storage-to-output, then other port/storage directions whose
declared input/output roles permit the read/write. Inputs cannot become assignment targets. Preserve
existing storage-only packed transfers and scalar-port behavior; the new check applies to
record-port copies, not retroactively to all aggregate storage assignments.

Reuse typed `+size` and explicit `+interface` carrier entries. Record member order is authored
order, first member most significant, as already implemented by
`AggregatePathSupport::record_member_low_offset`. Scalar paths retain their leaf widths and exact
packed ranges. No scalarized public field pins, payload register copies, implicit reset, added
pipeline edge or silent arbitration.

### Detached public metadata

Select optional `source.interface_ports` on successful directly parsed ISF check/semantic reports,
and `interface_ports` in schedule JSON. One producer must project fresh JSON-safe values from parsed
declared ports through native, API and actual newline MCP; it must not export parser/private IR
objects. Unrelated source formats and failure reports gain no invented ISF declarations. Unknown
declaration metadata in caller-created actors remains null, rather than reconstructed from inferred
hardware signals.

The snapshot orders inputs in their authored order followed by outputs in their authored order,
matching the existing parser handoff. Entries contain `name`, `direction`, `width`, and optional
authored `type` and resolved `type_kind`; named-domain entries also contain `domain`. A record adds
`fields`, an ordered array of scalar leaves with port-relative `path`, `width`, `lsb`, `msb`,
`signed`, and optional `state_model`. Nested paths follow the existing aggregate path syntax. The
normalized semantic type catalog remains the authority for recursive type declarations. Schedule
domain details carry the same snapshot for their declared ports. Generated private handoffs do not
appear as authored top ports. Advertise every added field family in the public capability contracts
and qualify detached values and complete report parity.

### Delivery and qualification order

1. Implement the detached metadata producer on the currently admitted scalar
   interface, with record-layout producer controls. Prove unchanged scheduled
   FSM and HDL; this preparatory slice does not admit record source ports.
2. Admit and qualify packed record inputs, scalar reads and input-to-storage
   whole copies. Cover local/imported/nested types, invalid paths/types, unused
   declarations, domains and generated children under their existing bounds.
3. Admit output records and whole copies only with sound physical writer
   ownership/admission, preserving unrelated scalar and storage controls.
4. Add scalar output-field writes after qualifying physical packed-range
   overlap. Whole-root/member overlap and generated competing writers must
   refuse unless a demonstrated compatibility/exclusion contract admits them.
5. Qualify affected backend profiles and the complete supplied consumer
   outcome. Direct SystemVerilog/Verilog and supported VHDL subsets have
   separate obligations; an unsupported profile must refuse precisely.

Input delivery does not depend on general independent-controller repairs. Output writes consume
those prerequisites only where their actual behavior needs them. Native HDL observations require
existing HIAL admission and failure-only observation; never replay a spent capture to seek
recurrence. Each implementation leaf may split further before source changes.

## Consequences at selection

R1–R3 remain unshipped until their owned slices and consumer qualification pass. R4/R5 stay
separately owned optional follow-ups after required duration/timer work; transaction-local aggregate
ports, banks and variant syntax are not implicitly admitted. The book keeps present support
boundaries and labels this selection as future work. No external corpus counts, timing guarantees,
runtime signoff or downstream integration completion follow from this decision.

Permanent qualification must include independently authored packed values, member-order/type
mismatch and input-write negatives, unchanged baseline controls, complete native/API/newline
products, supported corpus cases, capability/spec/book alignment and recoverable downstream response
evidence.

## Producer implementation evidence — 2026-09-30

SEM `.60.4.3.1.1` qualifies the detached producer independently of source admission and report
wiring. T1983 retains independently expected nested/imported ranges, signed/state-model leaves,
mutation isolation and invalid metadata. The draft's hostile controls found an argument-context
defect: a failed regex returns an empty list in list context, while an array returns its members.
Either can change the predicate/message argument slots of a validation helper. Predicates now return
explicit booleans or scalar counts; the helper also requires exact argument arity. This is a
producer repair, not a claim about uninspected validators or a public record-port implementation.

Reproduce the failed-regex mechanism independently:

```bash
perl -e 'sub predicate { $_[0] =~ /\A[01]\z/ } sub guard { print "arguments=",scalar(@_)," first=",($_[0] // "undef"),"\n" } guard(predicate(2), "error message"); guard(scalar(predicate(2)), "error message");'
```

The first call places the message in the predicate slot; the scalar call keeps both slots. The
permanent hostile controls verify refusal rather than accepting report parity as proof of valid
metadata. No native HDL runtime is established.

## Declaration report integration — 2026-09-30

SEM `.60.4.3.1.2` captures validated parser declarations before scheduler port injection. Ordinary
module IR carries a fresh closed snapshot; domain sources select their original owned entries.
Generated transaction children have unknown declaration metadata, rather than pretending private
ports are actor declarations. Reports distinguish known empty arrays from unknown null; unrelated
and failed source reports omit the ISF source field.

The shipped preparatory surfaces are success `source.interface_ports`, schedule `interface_ports`
and owned `clock_domains[].interface_ports`, with one complete shared discovery descriptor at
`source_optional_fields.interface_ports` and `schedule_report_interface_ports`. T1984 independently
expects local/imported scalar declarations, unused/undriven entries, source order and domain
ownership; actual event crossings and generated children demonstrate private-port exclusion. This
report delivery does not admit authored records. Complete transport and supported-corpus
qualification remains explicitly owned by `.60.4.3.1.3` before record input implementation. No
native HDL runtime is claimed.

## Complete metadata qualification — 2026-09-30

SEM `.60.4.3.1.3` qualifies complete typed native/API/actual newline products against independent
declaration witnesses. T1985 joins the live `build_source_query_cohort()` selector's ISF rows to
explicit reviewed source identities and declared port lists, then executes every applicable check,
semantic and schedule query. The selector owns supported catalog applicability; this is not a census
of product features, all repository fixtures or runtime coverage.
`feature.isf_declared_interface_metadata` now names this delivered metadata through the dedicated
`isf/interface_port_metadata.isf` fixture in the existing supported ISF pipeline corpus.

Local/imported aliases, unused/undriven declarations, known empty interfaces, a named empty domain,
malformed record/list/width refusals and unrelated FSM/PPIF reports receive complete transport
comparisons. Discovery compares complete native, in-process, API and newline sections. Canonical
typed JSON comparisons retain scalar kinds; shared field loss, wrong width/direction/order, private
data and stringified widths still fail independent expectations even when all three fabricated
transport copies agree. No parser or report values are repaired by the oracle. Source bytes remain
unchanged across queries.

Together with T1983/T1984 and the retained historical report/carrier/HDL controls, this closes the
preparatory declaration metadata lane. Authored record source ports and their hardware behavior
remain owned by the subsequent input/output leaves; no native HDL execution or complete consumer
delivery is established.

The corpus accounting control rejects duplicate `(relpath, classification, coverage)` tuples even
under different IDs. Reusing an existing source for the new identical contract failed that gate, so
the delivered metadata owns a separate runnable fixture. T248 also exposed stale exact expectations
from the prior storage-word-access entry (Git `3fa482924`, found with `git log -S`). The pre-slice
`241fad6b5` public catalog already exceeded those expectations; the new fixture adds only its
distinct entry. T248's exact census, tuple/ID and classification/strict checks and T1883's complete
cohort join retain the repair. Counts describe catalog entries, not independently implemented
features or runtime qualification. Recount from the live public catalog; do not reuse the old dated
qualification receipt as a current total.

## Record-input ingress selection — 2026-09-30

SEM `.60.4.3.2.1` traces the refused input boundary before widening it. Parser
`_finalize_actor_type_references` admits aggregate aliases only on storage;
`_validate_actor_aggregate_storage_paths`, rule operand maps and enum disambiguation currently
select storage roots. Adding inputs to one map is insufficient. Use a shared declaration-root
description, with transaction locals/formals and drive parameters masking outer names in their
actual scope. An input shadowed by a writable formal must not become that formal's role; an
unresolved local must not borrow its outer type or placeholder width. The existing formal resolver
and domain ownership remain authoritative.

Prepare a strict resolved-record identity gate separately from
`PayloadTypeSupport::payload_compatible_with_type_spec`. That public helper intentionally checks
payload shape and scalar width, allowing different signed and state-model facts. Preserve it for its
existing callers. Port copies compare recursive kinds, ordered record members, ordered list
children, widths, signed values and optional resolved state-model presence/value. Unspecified stays
unspecified; do not substitute a backend rendering default. Alias names are not part of resolved
identity. Malformed/unresolved roots fail contextually.

Transaction conditions, switch values, set/update RHS, rule guards/assignments, named-drive
bodies/actuals and inline drives need explicit scalar-versus-copy checks from the first admission.
Whole-record values are permitted only in qualified same-type assignments with allowed declaration
roles; expression operators, truthiness and subaggregate writes refuse. Existing storage-only packed
transfers retain their separate contract. Domain lookup resolves a path to its declared root,
honoring lexical masking and preserving the authored path in diagnostics; it must not invent a
crossing from a same-named formal.

The current aggregate validator handles `set`, but not `update` or `sample` leaf paths. Sampling
width collection copies exact root widths, not resolved leaf facts. Input delivery therefore owns
explicit scalar-leaf sampling in entry/body contexts, with resolved width/type and existing capture
timing. Whole-record sampling into an inferred alias remains outside this bounded delivery. No
hidden sample, delayed edge or new aggregate local is introduced. Typed `+size` and explicit
`+interface` already preserve unused declarations; generated/domain routes must retain those
identities before behavior signoff.

Reproduce the historical identity/refusal control at pre-admission revision
`0d01ca3fc8f880acf926ae59305843a1172bf1d3`, without HDL:

scripts/run_with_ram_guard.sh -- perl -Iperl -MFSM::Adapter::ISF -MFSM::Package::PayloadTypeSupport -MJSON::PP -e '

The input lane now separately owns closed gates, source admission, generated/ domain carriers and
independent HDL/public completion. This planning receipt does not establish new input acceptance,

mutation mechanism, not a new numeric value or public field contract.
